questions.question: What is √144?
questions.explain: A square root asks 'what number times itself gives 144?' — since 12 × 12 = 144, √144 = 12. The most common trap is halving (144 ÷ 2 = 72); taking a square root is the inverse of squaring, not dividing by 2.

questions.question: Léa builds a solid cube out of 64 linking cubes. What is ∛64, the number of cubes along one edge?
questions.explain: A cube root asks 'what number used three times gives 64?' — 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so ∛64 = 4. Watch out for answering 8 (that is √64, the square root) or 21.3 (that is 64 ÷ 3).

questions.question: √54 lies between which two whole numbers?
questions.explain: Find the nearest perfect squares below and above: 49 = 7² and 64 = 8², and 54 is between them, so √54 is between 7 and 8. The classic trap is halving 54 to get 26 and 27 — that is division, not a square root.

questions.question: A square patio is tiled with 400 small square tiles arranged 20 by 20, and 121 of them are grey. The grey part forms a smaller square. What is √(121/400), the fraction of the patio's side length that the grey square covers?
questions.explain: For a fraction, take the square root of the top and the bottom separately: √121 = 11 and √400 = 20, so √(121/400) = 11/20. The usual slip is rooting only one part of the fraction (121/20 or 11/200) — both numerator and denominator must be rooted.

questions.question: Estimate √75 to one decimal place.
questions.explain: √75 sits between √64 = 8 and √81 = 9, so test tenths: 8.6² = 73.96 and 8.7² = 75.69, and 75 is closer to 75.69, giving √75 ≈ 8.7. The trap is stopping at the first square below 75 and answering 8.6 without checking which neighbour is closer.

questions.question: Using prime factors, 1225 = 5 × 5 × 7 × 7. What is √1225?
questions.explain: Group the prime factors into identical pairs and take one factor from each pair: (5 × 5) and (7 × 7) give 5 × 7 = 35, so √1225 = 35. The most common mistake is adding the grouped factors (5 + 7 = 12) instead of multiplying them.

questions.question: Nima's cube-shaped aquarium has a volume of 27 000 cm³. He wants to run a plastic strip all the way around the square rim at the top. How long a strip does he need?
questions.explain: For a cube, edge = ∛volume, and ∛27 000 = 30 cm because 30 × 30 × 30 = 27 000; the top rim is a square, so its perimeter is 4 × 30 = 120 cm. Two traps here: dividing the volume by 3 (9000 cm) instead of taking a cube root, and stopping at the edge length (30 cm) without finding the perimeter.

questions.question: The square skateboard pad at Maya's Burnaby park has an area of 100 m². The city wants to rebuild it as a square pad with double the area. What will the new side length be, to one decimal place?
questions.explain: Double the area first (100 × 2 = 200 m²), then take the square root: 14.1² = 198.81 and 14.2² = 201.64, so √200 ≈ 14.1 m. The big misconception is doubling the side to 20 m — that would give an area of 400 m², four times the original, because area grows with the square of the side.
